about.title: La Habra Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: La Habra property owners, from shopping centers along Whittier Boulevard to residential complexes near Lambert Road, are expected to keep their premises reasonably safe for visitors. When a wet floor, broken sidewalk slab, poor lighting, or hidden hazard causes a fall, the property owner or manager may be responsible if they knew about the danger, or reasonably should have known, and failed to fix it or warn people in time. These cases often hinge on details that disappear quickly: surveillance footage gets overwritten, spills get mopped up, and memories fade. If you were injured in a fall anywhere in La Habra, contacting us soon after the incident can make a meaningful difference in preserving evidence and understanding what your claim may involve. We handle slip and fall cases directly and work to help you understand your legal options.

whyChoose.title: Why La Habra Residents Choose Us

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. We can help gather maintenance logs, complaint history, and inspection records to establish this.

items.title: Video and Evidence Fade Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage at stores and apartment complexes is often erased within days or weeks. Acting quickly gives us the best chance to request and preserve that footage before it's gone.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: Even if you're partly blamed for not seeing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule generally still allows a claim, though your share of fault may reduce compensation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in La Habra?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a lawsuit, though claims against a public entity (like a city-owned sidewalk) usually require a much shorter notice period. It's best to talk with us as soon as possible so no deadlines are missed.

items.question: What if I fell at a business near La Habra Boulevard or Imperial Highway and no one else saw it happen?
items.answer: Lack of witnesses doesn't automatically end a claim. Store surveillance cameras, incident reports, and physical evidence like torn clothing or the hazard itself can still support your case. We can help identify what evidence exists and act quickly to request it.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to work with us?
items.answer: No. We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost for a free case review and no obligation to move forward.
